text: In 1791, authorities in France suppressed Justine or the Misfortunes of Virtue. In March 1801 the stocks of The New Justine and Juliette were seized when Sade was arrested at his publisher's office. The Cour Royale de Paris ordered the book's destruction on 19 May 1815.

text: The Decameron was among the works burned in Florence in 1497 in a bonfire incited by Girolamo Savonarola. It was placed on the Index of 1559 under the instructions of Paul IV, and its prohibition was confirmed in the Index of 1564. In 1573 Pope Gregory XIII commissioned a revised edition in which the clergymen were replaced with secular people.

text: The Chinese government banned Zhuan Falun and other publications on 24 July 1996. On 26 July 1999 the Ministry of Public Security called for the confiscation and destruction of all publications related to Falun Gong. By 30 July, Xinhua had reported confiscations of over one million Falun Gong books and other materials.

text: Random House cancelled the 2008 release of The Jewel of Medina by Sherry Jones over concerns about possible inflammatory content. The government banned The Jewel of Medina in Malaysia in 2009.

text: In July 2007, the bookseller Borders moved The Adventures of Tintin in the Congo by Hergé to an area reserved for adult graphic novels, and Waterstone's followed suit. In 2007, the Brooklyn Public Library removed the book from public display and kept it locked in a back room. In August 2007 a student filed a complaint in Brussels demanding a ban, and in February 2012 the court ruled that the book would not be banned. In September 2011 the book was removed from a children's library in Kulturhuset in Stockholm.

text: The novel Call Me By Your Name by André Aciman was hidden from sale by the online store Labirint in December 2022. In January 2023 the book was permanently banned from libraries and classrooms in St. Johns County School District, and in September 2023 it was banned from libraries and classrooms in Matanuska-Susitna Borough School District. In June 2025 the state Education Commissioner wrote to the Hillsborough County school district that the book and one other were "pornographic", and the district superintendent was called to a Florida board of education meeting on June 4 about them.
